NONE: › (used when writing some languages) a ~ mark made above a letter, especially n, to show that the letter has a special sound
齶化符號，鼻音化符號（~）
› a thin, usually square or rectangular piece of baked clay, plastic, etc. used for covering roofs, floors, walls, etc.
瓦片；瓷磚
› to cover a wall or floor with tiles
給…鋪瓦；給…貼瓷磚

example: roof tiles
屋頂瓦
floor tiles
地磚
ceramic tiles
瓷磚
carpet tiles
地毯片
We're going to tile the bathroom.
我們要給浴室貼瓷磚。

NONE: › (of a surface) covered with tiles
（表面）鋪瓦的，鋪磚的

example: The kitchen has a tiled floor.
廚房地面鋪了地磚。

NONE: › a person who fixes tiles to a surface
泥瓦匠；鋪瓦工；貼磚工

example: Can you recommend a good tiler?
你能介紹一個好的瓦匠嗎？

NONE: A2 up to (the time that); until
直到；到…為止
› the drawer in a cash register (= a machine which records sales in a shop, and in which money is kept) or the cash register itself
收銀機的抽屜；收銀機
› to prepare and use land for growing crops
耕，犁（土地）

example: We waited till six thirty for you.
我們一直等你到六點半。
Up till 1918, women in Britain were not allowed to vote.
在1918年以前，英國不允許婦女參加選舉。
How long is it till the baby is due?
你還有多久生孩子？
Next time you have the till open, could you give me some change?
下次打開收銀機時，你給我些零錢好嗎？
I think these items have been rung up wrongly on the till.
我想這些商品在收銀機上記錯了。
This piece of land has been tilled for hundreds of years.
這塊土地已經被耕耘了幾百年。

NONE: › a roll of paper on which the separate amounts of money paid for goods are recorded in a shop's cash register
（記錄售出物品金額的）收銀機捲紙
› for ever
無休止地

example: I don't want to have to wait till kingdom come for you to make up your mind.
我可不想無休止地等你立定主意。

NONE: › for a very long time
長時間地；很久

example: I could sit here and argue with you till the cows come home, but it wouldn't solve anything.
我可以坐在這裡無休止地跟你爭論下去，但那樣解決不了任何問題。

NONE: › a long handle attached to and used to turn a rudder (= blade at the back of a boat used to control the boat's direction)
舵柄
› to (cause to) move into a sloping position
（使）傾斜
› a sloping position or a move in a particular direction, especially up or down
傾斜，傾側

example: He tilted his chair backwards and put his feet up on his desk.
他把椅子向後傾，雙腳擱在書桌上。
Anna looked up at him with her head tilted to one side.
安娜歪著腦袋，抬眼望著他。
The front seats of the car tilt.
汽車的前座可以傾斜。
She wore her hat at a tilt.
她歪戴著帽子。
figurative There has been a tilt to/towards/away from thesocialists among some groups of young people.
在一些青年團體中，存在著一種親／反社會主義的傾向。

NONE: › to fight enemies who do not really exist
向風車挑戰；跟實際不存在的敵人戰鬥
› If something tilts the balance, it is the thing that causes a particular situation to happen or a particular decision to be made when other situations or decisions are possible.
打破平衡／使天平傾斜；起決定性作用

example: This might just tilt the balance in the government's favour.
這樣或許正好打破平衡，使形勢有利於政府一方。
